I am a William H. Kruskal Instructor of Statistics at the University of Chicago.
I previously completed my PhD in biostatistics at Harvard University where I was
advised by Rafael Irizarry and Jeff Miller. 

My research interests lie at the intersection of high-dimensional statistics and genomics. My recent work includes:

1.  Dimensionality reduction for single-cell genomic data
2.  Manifold learning for spatial transcriptomics
3.  Integration of high-dimensional random matrices
4.  Estimation of perturbation effects in CRISPR data

Email: pnicol\@uchicago.edu
